plainTitle: A 14-storey building with shops and a bigger park at Danforth Road and Birchmount Road

sources.label: Staff report from the Director, Community Planning, Scarborough District

whatIsProposed.text: City Council changed the zoning rules for 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road. This allows a 14-storey building with homes above and shops on the ground floor.

citations.quote: City Council amend City of Toronto Zoning By-law 569-2013, as amended, for the lands municipally known as 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road
to permit the development of a 14 storey mixed used building (plus mechanical penthouse)

whatIsProposed.text: The plan has about 524 homes and 1,563 square metres of retail space.
whatIsProposed.caveat: The staff report gives two different home counts: 524 in some places and 526 in others. The record does not explain the difference.

citations.quote: a 14 storey mixed used building at 468 to 480 Danforth Road with a total of 524 units and 1,563 square metres of retail gross floor area
The proposal contains a total of 526 residential units and 1,563 square metres of ground floor retail.

whatIsProposed.text: The building steps down to lower heights at its edges: 4 storeys next to the park, 8 storeys along Birchmount Road and 6 storeys along Danforth Road.

citations.quote: The proposal has a maximum height of 14 storeys (53.5 meters)
The built form transition s down to 4 storeys (19 met res) fronting Sadler Parkette

whatIsProposed.text: The owner must give the City land to make the nearby Sadler Parkette bigger. Council set a minimum of 742 square metres. The plan describes about 754 square metres, including the whole lot at 509 Birchmount Road, where a house now stands.

citations.quote: the Owner shall convey to the City an on-site parkland dedication, having a minimum size of 742 square metres
The proposal also provides approximately 754 square metres of on-site parkland dedication that would expand the adjacent Sadler Parkette
The portion of the subject site known as 509 Birchmount Road is currently occupied by a single-storey detached dwelling.

whatIsProposed.text: The plan includes 340 car parking spaces, mostly in a two-level underground garage, and 394 bicycle parking spaces.

citations.quote: The proposal includes a total of 340 vehicular parking spaces, of which, 330 parking spaces are proposed in a two level underground parking garage.
A total of 394 bicycle parking spaces are proposed

why.text: The site is zoned for commercial use only. The zoning allows no homes and a height of up to 11 metres, so a zoning change was needed.

citations.quote: The CR zoning category permits commercial uses with a maximum height of 11 metres
there is no density permissions allocated to residential uses on the site

why.text: City staff supported the application. They said it fits provincial policy and the City's Official Plan, and that the site has transit on both roads.
why.caveat: This is the opinion of City staff.

citations.quote: The proposed Zoning By-law Amendment application is consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement (2024) and conforms to the City's Official Plan.
it is serviced by public transit on both Birchmount Road and Danforth Road

why.text: The site now has a one-storey plaza that held a grocery store, which has closed. The new retail space is smaller than today's, but staff say it is big enough for a food store. The applicant told staff it is talking with a grocer.

citations.quote: While the grocery store has officially closed, the remaining commercial/retail businesses continue to operate.
it is generally large enough to accommodate a food store, or another significant retail/commercial space
The applicant has advised they are in discussion with a grocer to tenant this space.

whoIsAffected.text: The site is at the corner of Danforth Road and Birchmount Road, in Ward 20 (Scarborough Southwest).

citations.quote: The subject site is located within the diagonal intersection of Danforth Road and Birchmount Road
Ward: 20 - Scarborough Southwest

whoIsAffected.text: The businesses still operating in the existing plaza. The new building would replace the existing one-storey building.
whoIsAffected.caveat: The record does not say what happens to the current businesses or when.

citations.quote: 468 to 480 Danforth Road contains a single storey building with a staggered front elevation

whoIsAffected.text: Neighbours to the north and users of Sadler Parkette: the building would cast some shadow there. Staff said the shadows are similar to what an 8-storey building following City guidelines would cause, and found them acceptable.
whoIsAffected.caveat: This is the opinion of City staff.

citations.quote: The proposed building results in some shadow on Neighbourhoods to the north of the site.
thus the resulting shadow impacts are considered acceptable

whoIsAffected.text: Families with school-age children: the public school board said local schools may not have room for more students. The Catholic board said its local elementary school has room.

citations.quote: the local elementary and secondary schools may not have sufficient space to accommodate additional students
the local Catholic elementary school ha s sufficient space to accommodate additional students

whoIsAffected.text: Drivers in the area: the building is expected to add 250 to 310 car trips in rush hours. Staff accepted a study saying the effect on traffic would be minor.

citations.quote: The site is anticipated to generate a total of 250 and 310 new two-way vehicle trips
Site-generated traffic impacts at signalized intersections within the study area are anticipated to be minor.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The owner may build better-than-basic park features. In return, the City would reduce part of the owner's development charges (fees for parks and recreation).

citations.quote: City Council approve a development charge credit against the Parks and Recreation component of the Development Charges for the design and construction by the Owner of the Above Base Park Improvements

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Council asked staff to explore with the owner a possible package of community benefits, which may include public art. Staff are to report back on any offer.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: This is a request to explore. The record does not say what, if anything, will be provided.

citations.quote: to work with the Owner to explore the feasibility of an in-kind community benefit package
that may include the provision of Public Art

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The detailed design still needs site plan approval. No site plan application had been filed when the report was written.

citations.quote: The proposal is subject to Site Plan Control. A Site Plan application has not been submitted.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Council approved a revised version of the draft zoning by-law, not the version first attached to the staff report.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: This page has not compared the two versions.

citations.quote: substantially in accordance with the draft Zoning By-law Amendment included as revised Attachment 5
Staff recommend that Council approve the Zoning By-law Amendment application.

committee.text: Scarborough Community Council held the required public meeting and recommended approval without changes.

citations.quote: The Scarborough Community Council held a statutory public meeting on May 28, 2026
This item was considered by the Scarborough Community Council on May 28, 2026 and adopted without amendment.

council.text: City Council approved the zoning change without changes and without debate.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on June 24 and 25, 2026 without amendments and without debate.

whatHappensNext.text: The City's item page links this decision to By-law 617-2026. Next, the detailed design goes through site plan review, where staff say they will settle details such as wind measures and tree planting.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The record does not give a construction start date. This page has not checked whether anyone appealed.

citations.quote: See also By-law 617-2026
Any necessary mitigation measures will be determined and secured through the Site Plan application process.
